hooks.pinpoint_note: Verified 2026-09-09 against the published PDF fetched from the row's own source_url (ec.europa.eu/newsroom/just/document.cfm?doc_id=47711, 1,137,918 bytes, pdftotext -layout pages 8–11): criterion 4 begins on printed page 9 immediately after criterion 3's paragraph; the hospital/private-investigator sentence and footnote 14 ('See e.g. recitals 75, 76, 92, 116.') sit on page 9; the sentence 'Beyond these provisions… rights and freedoms | of individuals.' breaks across the 9/10 page boundary, so the page-9 example sentence is the anchor. The nine criteria sit in the body under 'a) When is a DPIA mandatory?' (§III.B, page 8), NOT an annex — the ratified prose's 'Annex 1, criterion 4' label is the approved text and is left untouched, exactly as 718bb432's 'Annex 1, criterion 3' was (doc 242 Q5). Bare ref '9' per the doc 242 Q5 convention.
hooks.atoms_rationale: required_atoms = the coarse jurisdiction gate only, exactly as doc 233 §10b's card specifies ('coarse eligibility gate only (GDPR jurisdiction)'); the card itself records that the atom grammar has no OR operator, so the gate nominates on any EU-GDPR DPIA record — accepted as the card states it, not worked around. fact_atoms = the intake's own WP248-criterion-4 reason ('Sensitive or highly personal data' → slug sensitive_data, dpia-reasons-vocabulary.ts): the same WP248-criterion-N ↔ intake-reason-N mapping the sibling criterion-3 hook uses through class:employee_monitoring (rule-states.ts derives that class from the systematic_monitoring reason, first priority), expressible directly as a state: atom now that doc 241 added DPIA's reasons_to_conduct paths to STATE_ATOM_ENUMS. Consequence: S1 renders iff the customer selected that reason (any obligation verdict); a record listing health/financial/location categories WITHOUT the reason is `unknown` → omitted (accepted posture), and the two-leg selection cannot rescue it because the only selectable atom does not hold. Alternatives NOT chosen (a data-only UPDATE to revise; flagged for the orchestrator/CEO because doc 233 §10b left the firing condition 'for whoever wires this hook's required_atoms for real'): (a) flag:special_category alone — fires only on the 'Health or medical data' category (rule-states.ts flagsFrom), narrower than the paragraph; (b) several category atoms (special_category/biometric/Financial data/Location data) — AND semantics for a deterministic 'same', every partial match becomes an AI two-leg selection / ROO. A UK-GDPR-only record does not nominate this hook (same as 718bb432).
hooks.distinguishing_note: none — the panel's CORRECTED mechanism (doc 233 §10b, DRAFTED 2026-09-09): a distinguishing pair on an accepted-posture hook omits the WHOLE hook (directionFor: accepted + different → omit; a holding pair forces 'different'), so financial/location data are folded into the single unconditional S1 paragraph instead; distinguishing_atoms [] / distinguishing_pairs null / not_distinguishable true
hooks.code_gaps_checked: (1) R_ART_9_SPECIAL_CATEGORIES (engagement-map.ts ~line 527) still decides status from article_9_condition + looksHealth/looksBiometric only and never consults hasSpecialCat / the data_categories checkbox array — re-confirmed in code 2026-09-09; NOT a blocker for this hook: nothing in its wiring reads a state:engagement_map.* atom (the ruling forbids gating on rule status), and the engagement-map status is not an input to nomination/agreement. It remains the separate customer-facing Section 2 defect the panel flagged. (2) DPIA_DATA_CATS (intake-contracts/dpia-framework.ts) has no criminal-conviction/offence option — re-confirmed; NOT a blocker for this wiring because the firing atom is the reasons_to_conduct option 'Sensitive or highly personal data' (WP248 criterion 4's own heading, whose text expressly covers Article 10 data), not a data_category atom, and Article 10 is unconditional content in the paragraph per the ruling. It DOES mean no atom can ever distinguish an Article-10-only record from an Article-9 one, so the panel's 'fact-gateable signal' caveat stands unresolved — an intake gap, not worked around here.

profile.rule_statement: Sensitive data or data of a highly personal nature — special categories of personal data under Article 9 and personal data relating to criminal convictions or offences under Article 10, and beyond those provisions other categories of data that increase the possible risk to individuals' rights and freedoms (Recital 75) — is one of the WP248 criteria indicating processing likely to result in high risk, and supports finding a DPIA obligation under Article 35 GDPR (WP248 rev.01, criterion 4, page 9).
profile.curation_note: Doc 233 §10b (WP248 rev.01 criterion 4 — sensitive data or data of a highly personal nature; adopted 4 Oct 2017, EDPB-endorsed 25 May 2018). Three-lawyer panel ruling 2026-09-09 (CEO-authorised per charter), unanimous both rounds: NOT suppressed — no engagement-map rule keys on this row (R_ART_9_SPECIAL_CATEGORIES reads only article_9_condition + health/biometric regex, never the data_categories checkbox; R_ART_35_3_B requires large scale as a hard conjunct; nothing tests Article 10 data); do not add to DPIA_ENGAGEMENT_MAP_SUPPRESSED_SOURCE_IDS. Accepted posture: WP248 stating a general criterion, not an adverse finding. Mechanism as CORRECTED by the panel's drafting round: NO distinguishing_atoms/pairs (accepted + different → the whole hook omits), not_distinguishable = true; financial and location data folded into the single unconditional S1 paragraph, grounded in GDPR Recital 75 via WP248's own footnote 14. Factor: the existing generic obligation factor (a split-out 'sensitive-data trigger' factor is a [NEEDS: CEO ruling] the card left open). required_atoms = coarse GDPR-jurisdiction gate only (the card's own instruction; no OR operator exists). fact_atoms = the intake's own 'Sensitive or highly personal data' reason (state:intake.reasons_to_conduct.sensitive_data=true) — the sibling criterion-3 mapping (WP248 criterion N ↔ intake reason N); see tests/fixtures/doc233/hooks.json 118b22d4.atoms_rationale for the alternatives. Pinpoint: printed page 9 of the published PDF (body §III.B.a 'When is a DPIA mandatory?', not an annex), verified against the PDF fetched from this row's source_url 2026-09-09; anchor = the hospital/private-investigator sentence (position 429 in excerpt_text). Doc 233 §10b's own 'CEO: ratify / revise / retire' line is blank; ratification instructed by the orchestrator's 2026-09-09 brief. Profile created by the §10b hook-authoring pass (doc 239's batch excluded #10b pending prose). Known, unresolved intake gap: DPIA_DATA_CATS has no criminal-offence option, so Article 10 data can never be a fact-gateable signal — unconditional content only, per the ruling.
